LOG_LEVEL.description: Logging verbosity. Use 'debug' to diagnose tool dispatch or GitLab API issues; use 'warn' or 'error' for low-noise production runs.

GITLAB_URL.description: GitLab instance URL, e.g. https://gitlab.com or https://gitlab.example.com. Must include http:// or https://. Defaults to GitLab.com.

AUTO_UPDATE.description: Self-update mode. 'true' downloads and applies the newest release on start; 'check' only logs availability; 'false' disables it. Keep 'false' in containers because the filesystem is ephemeral.

GITLAB_TOKEN.description: GitLab Personal Access Token with the scopes required by the operations you intend to call. Use 'api' for full functionality; narrower read-only setups can use scopes such as read_api, read_user, read_repository, or read_registry depending on the tools you need. Format: glpat-XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX.

TOOL_SURFACE.description: Canonical tool catalog selector. 'dynamic' is recommended for Glama and exposes the low-token gitlab_find_action + gitlab_execute_tool workflow. 'meta' exposes domain meta-tools. 'individual' exposes the full individual tool catalog and can be very large.

EXCLUDE_TOOLS.description: Comma-separated list of MCP tool names to exclude from registration, e.g. gitlab_admin,gitlab_runner. Useful for hiding high-risk or irrelevant domains.

RATE_LIMIT_RPS.description: Per-server tools/call rate limit in requests per second. '0' disables rate limiting. Use a positive number to protect shared or constrained GitLab instances.

AUTO_UPDATE_REPO.description: GitHub repository slug used for release assets when AUTO_UPDATE is enabled. Keep the default for official releases.

GITLAB_READ_ONLY.description: When 'true', disables every mutating tool at startup. Only read-only list/get/search-style operations remain. Recommended for exploratory, public, or untrusted-LLM scenarios.

GITLAB_SAFE_MODE.description: Dry-run mode. Mutating tools stay visible but return a structured JSON preview instead of executing. Read-only tools run normally. If GITLAB_READ_ONLY=true, read-only mode takes precedence.

RATE_LIMIT_BURST.description: Token-bucket burst size used when RATE_LIMIT_RPS is greater than 0. Must be at least 1 when rate limiting is enabled.

GITLAB_ENTERPRISE.description: Enable GitLab Premium/Ultimate tools. Set to 'true' only when the target instance supports Premium/Ultimate features, or when using GitLab.com with those capabilities.

META_PARAM_SCHEMA.description: Meta-tool input schema strategy for TOOL_SURFACE=meta. 'opaque' keeps tools/list compact; 'compact' includes action parameter names and simple types; 'full' includes full per-action JSON Schemas and costs significantly more tokens. Has little practical effect in dynamic mode.

CAPABILITY_SURFACE.description: Resource and prompt catalog selector. 'full' registers all resources, prompts, workflow guides, and schema resources. 'minimal' keeps the smallest capability surface; dynamic mode still returns action schemas inline.

EMBEDDED_RESOURCES.description: When 'true', get-style tool results include EmbeddedResource content blocks with canonical gitlab:// resource URIs. Set to 'false' for clients that do not tolerate duplicate or embedded content blocks.

AUTO_UPDATE_TIMEOUT.description: Pre-start auto-update download timeout. Valid range is 5s to 10m. Mostly irrelevant when AUTO_UPDATE=false.

AUTO_UPDATE_INTERVAL.description: Periodic update check interval for HTTP-mode background checks. Mostly irrelevant when AUTO_UPDATE=false.

GITLAB_IGNORE_SCOPES.description: Skip Personal Access Token scope detection and register all tools regardless of token permissions. API calls may still fail with 403 if the token lacks the required GitLab scopes.

UPLOAD_MAX_FILE_SIZE.description: Maximum file size for upload tools. Accepts bytes or human-friendly suffixes such as KB, MB, or GB. Upper bound is 1TB.

GITLAB_SKIP_TLS_VERIFY.description: Skip TLS certificate verification for self-signed certificates or internal CAs. Use only when you trust the network path to GITLAB_URL.

GITLAB_MCP_ALLOWED_IMPORT_DIRS.description: Additional OS path-list-separated directories allowed for project/group import archives passed by file path. Current working directory and OS temp directory are always allowed. Archives must resolve inside an allowed directory and use .tar.gz.

servers.description: A Model Context Protocol server that provides browser automation capabilities using Playwright, enabling LLMs to interact with web pages through structured accessibility snapshots without requiring screenshots or vision models.

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_CAPS.description: Comma-separated list of additional capabilities to enable, possible values: vision, pdf, devtools.

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_HOST.description: Host to bind server to. Default is localhost. Use 0.0.0.0 to bind to all interfaces.

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_PORT.description: Port to listen on for SSE transport.

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_BROWSER.description: Browser or chrome channel to use, possible values: chrome, firefox, webkit, msedge.

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_CODEGEN.description: Specify the language to use for code generation, possible values: "typescript", "none". Default is "typescript".

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_SANDBOX.description: Enable the sandbox for all process types that are normally not sandboxed.

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_SECRETS.description: Path to a file containing secrets in the dotenv format.

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_ENDPOINT.description: Bound browser endpoint to connect to.

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_HEADLESS.description: Run browser in headless mode, headed by default.

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_ISOLATED.description: Keep the browser profile in memory, do not save it to disk.

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_EXTENSION.description: Connect to a running browser instance (Edge/Chrome only). Requires the "Playwright Extension" to be installed.

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_INIT_PAGE.description: Path to TypeScript file to evaluate on Playwright page object.

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_CDP_HEADER.description: CDP headers to send with the connect request, multiple can be specified.

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_NO_SANDBOX.description: Disable the sandbox for all process types that are normally sandboxed.

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_OUTPUT_DIR.description: Path to the directory for output files.

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_CDP_TIMEOUT.description: Timeout in milliseconds for connecting to CDP endpoint, defaults to 30000ms.

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_INIT_SCRIPT.description: Path to JavaScript file to add as an initialization script. The script will be evaluated in every page before any of the page's scripts. Can be specified multiple times.

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_OUTPUT_MODE.description: Whether to save snapshots, console messages, network logs to a file or to the standard output. Can be "file" or "stdout". Default is "stdout".

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_PROXY_BYPASS.description: Comma-separated domains to bypass proxy, for example ".com,chromium.org,.domain.com".

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_PROXY_SERVER.description: Specify proxy server, for example "http://myproxy:3128" or "socks5://myproxy:8080".

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_SAVE_SESSION.description: Whether to save the Playwright MCP session into the output directory.

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS.description: Comma-separated list of hosts this server is allowed to serve from. Defaults to the host the server is bound to. Pass '*' to disable the host check.

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_CONSOLE_LEVEL.description: Level of console messages to return: "error", "warning", "info", "debug". Each level includes the messages of more severe levels.

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_SNAPSHOT_MODE.description: When taking snapshots for responses, specifies the mode to use. Can be "full" or "none". Default is "full".

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_STORAGE_STATE.description: Path to the storage state file for isolated sessions.

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_USER_DATA_DIR.description: Path to the user data directory. If not specified, a temporary directory will be created.

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_VIEWPORT_SIZE.description: Specify browser viewport size in pixels, for example "1280x720".

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_TIMEOUT_ACTION.description: Specify action timeout in milliseconds, defaults to 5000ms.

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS.description: Semicolon-separated list of TRUSTED origins to allow the browser to request. Default is to allow all. Important: *does not* serve as a security boundary and *does not* affect redirects.

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_BLOCKED_ORIGINS.description: Semicolon-separated list of origins to block the browser from requesting. Blocklist is evaluated before allowlist. If used without the allowlist, requests not matching the blocklist are still allowed. Important: *does not* serve as a security boundary and *does not* affect redirects.

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_IMAGE_RESPONSES.description: Whether to send image responses to the client. Can be "allow" or "omit", Defaults to "allow".

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_GRANT_PERMISSIONS.description: List of permissions to grant to the browser context, for example "geolocation", "clipboard-read", "clipboard-write".

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_TEST_ID_ATTRIBUTE.description: Specify the attribute to use for test ids, defaults to "data-testid".

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_TIMEOUT_NAVIGATION.description: Specify navigation timeout in milliseconds, defaults to 60000ms.

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_SHARED_BROWSER_CONTEXT.description: Reuse the same browser context between all connected HTTP clients.

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_ALLOW_UNRESTRICTED_FILE_A.description: Allow access to files outside of the workspace roots. Also allows unrestricted access to file:// URLs. By default access to file system is restricted to workspace root directories (or cwd if no roots are configured) only, and navigation to file:// URLs is blocked.

TAG_MATCH_BOOST.description: Score boost for exact tag matches in recall results. Higher = stronger tag priority.

MEMORY_HALF_LIFE_WEEKS.description: Weeks until memory importance decays to 50%. Longer = slower decay.

MEMORY_SEMANTIC_WEIGHT.description: Balance between semantic similarity (0.7) and decayed importance (0.3) in recall ranking.

ENABLE_CONSOLIDATE_TOOL.description: Enable the consolidate_context tool for retrospective memory extraction. Options: true, false.

EXTRACT_COMPLEX_CONCEPTS.description: Enable extraction of modifier+noun phrases (e.g., 'optimized WGSL'). Options: true, false.

MEMORY_CONSOLIDATION_FACTOR.description: Strength of access-based consolidation. Higher = frequently-used memories resist decay more.
